source_policy: Primary references support definitions and stated conditions. Bounded models, workshop stories and worked derivations are originally authored constructed examples. No production measurements or historical priority claims are presented.
purpose: Follow a previous volume through retention and refill into the next exact completed-round state.
meaning: A recurrence defines successive states from earlier ones and initial data. The workshop model separates retained old water from newly added water. Its numbered graph shows actual integer-round states instead of inventing fractional iterations.

definition.setting: A first-order affine recurrence for retained water followed by a fixed refill at discrete completed rounds.

signature.d: Litres added after retention in each completed round.
signature.vₙ: Volume after n completed rounds in litres.
signature.vₙ₋₁: Previous volume before the last completed round, for n>0.
signature.r vₙ₋₁: Retained contribution in the last completed round, for n>0.

conditions: Start with v₀ litres, where 0≤v₀≤40 L. Each completed round first retains fraction r of the current volume and then adds d litres.
Use 0≤r≤1 and 0≤d≤5 L. The number n of completed rounds is an integer from zero to twelve.
The rule is vₖ₊₁=r vₖ+d for integer k≥0. Changing r smoothly recalculates exact integer-round states; it does not create fractional rounds.
At n=0 the result is v₀ and no last transition has occurred. Last-transition retained and added contributions are therefore zero.
Allowed states stay between zero and 100 L: retention cannot increase the current volume and twelve refills add at most 60 L to at most 40 L initially.
definition.domain_notes: A recurrence needs a stated rule and initial data. This executable family uses one previous state and an affine update. The finite geometric sum is empty at n=0. At r=1 the result is v₀+nd without division by 1−r.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources; restricted-family properties are author-derived. Independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Begin at v₀. For each integer k from zero to n−1, set vₖ₊₁=r vₖ+d. Equivalently, vₙ=rⁿv₀+d∑ from j=0 to n−1 of rʲ. At n=0 return v₀; at r=1 use vₙ=v₀+nd.
grammar.precedence: Multiply the previous state by r before adding d; repeat the complete update exactly n times.

prompts.prompt: Why does the operation order matter?
prompts.answer: Retaining then refilling gives r v+d. Refilling first gives r(v+d), which also reduces the new refill.
Not in this model: each round is one whole application of the stated rule.
